name: sha2-with-c-intrinsic (AWS Crypto Algorithms Group)
baseline: OpenSSL SHA-256/SHA-512 (SHA Extensions assembly path, commit 13c5d744)
workload: SHA-256 and SHA-512 compression benchmarked on message sizes from 1 to 65536 bytes, isolated per function, 25 warm-up + 100 timed iterations averaged, min of 10 repeats reported, in raw CPU cycles.
claimed_speedup: SHA-256 w/ Intel SHA Extensions, 65536-byte input: 183,685 cycles (their C intrinsics) vs 198,528 cycles (OpenSSL SHA-NI asm) = ~1.08x faster (derived from page data). Their generic/AVX/AVX2/AVX-512 C paths are NOT faster than OpenSSL's corresponding avx/avx2 asm paths on the same table (e.g. avx2 (C) 709,146 cycles vs avx2 (ossl) 620,729 cycles at 65536 bytes -- OpenSSL wins there).
compiler_and_flags: clang-9, -O2/Release (CMake Release build); repo also built/tested with gcc-9
hardware: Dell XPS 13 7390 2-in-1, Intel Core i7-1065G7 (Ice Lake), Turbo Boost off, Ubuntu 18.04.2 LTS
tradeoffs: Provides only raw compression functions (no padding/state management, no shared/static lib); explicitly a benchmarking/compiler-research sample, not intended for production use. Requires SHA_NI/AVX/AVX2/AVX512 capable CPU and matching compiler intrinsics support.
caveats: Mixed result: only the SHA-Extensions code path beats OpenSSL (~8% at large inputs); the plain AVX/AVX2 C intrinsics paths are slower than OpenSSL's own AVX/AVX2 asm on the same benchmark table. Numbers are from 2020 against an OpenSSL dev commit, not a released OpenSSL version; repo has had no commits since 2020 (abandoned). Author affiliation (AWS Crypto Algorithms Group / Gueron & Drucker) lends credibility despite inactivity.

name: blake2_simd (blake2b_simd / blake2s_simd)
workload: Long in-memory inputs hashed with various hash functions (BLAKE3, blake2s_simd, blake2b_simd variants, libsodium BLAKE2b, OpenSSL SHA-1/SHA-512), median cycles-per-byte reported by the bench_multiprocess sub-crate averaging over many runs.
claimed_speedup: blake2b_simd BLAKE2b: 2.81 cpb vs OpenSSL SHA-512: 5.11 cpb (~1.8x faster, derived from page data); blake2b_simd many::hash / BLAKE2bp: 1.43-1.44 cpb vs OpenSSL SHA-512 5.11 cpb (~3.5x, derived) and vs OpenSSL SHA-1 3.51 cpb (~2.4-2.5x, derived). Also beats libsodium's own BLAKE2b (3.07 cpb) by a smaller margin.
compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.40.0, clang 9.0.1 (clang used to build the OpenSSL/libsodium comparison bindings); `cargo run --release`
tradeoffs: Different hash algorithm (BLAKE2 vs SHA-2/SHA-1), so not a drop-in replacement -- callers must accept BLAKE2 digests instead of SHA output. Rust crate; usable from C++ only via FFI/cbindgen, not a native C/C++ API. libsodium versions used (1.0.18) and OpenSSL (1.1.1.d) are from 2019.
caveats: Benchmark numbers are from ~2019/2020 (rustc 1.40, OpenSSL 1.1.1.d, libsodium 1.0.18); OpenSSL has since gained further SHA-NI/AVX-512 tuning in 3.x so the exact margin vs current OpenSSL is unverified, though BLAKE2's structural throughput advantage over SHA-2 on non-SHA-NI-favorable inputs is well established. Single-machine, single-run-class result (Tier A on methodology completeness, not independently reproduced elsewhere).
